title: fix(objectql): an item registered through the registry path is served with its package's `_packageVersion`
body:
Fixes #22689

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`_packageVersion` is declared on the spec's protection envelope (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`: "Owning package version."). The metadata plugin's artifact loader stamps it through `applyProtection(item, { packageId, packageVersion })`. The registry load path, `ObjectQL.registerApp(manifest)` into `SchemaRegistry.registerItem` / `registerObject`, called `applyProtection(item, { packageId })` and stamped the id alone. The comment above that call said both paths "produce identical lock state". They did not: `GET /api/v1/meta/app` served a registry-registered app with `_packageId` and no `_packageVersion`, so a console waiting on an upgrade could not tell the new app from the old one a stale kernel still serves (the upgrade case behind objectstack-ai/objectui#12087).

Premise checked on `origin/main` `61bea242`: both `applyProtection` sites in `registry.ts` passed `{ packageId }` only. Measured before the change: the served app had `_packageVersion` undefined (ablation A below is that reading).

## How `registerItem` learns the version

The caller hands it in. `SchemaRegistry.registerItem`, `registerObject` and `registerApp` take an optional trailing `packageVersion` argument, and both `applyProtection` calls pass `{ packageId, packageVersion }`. No version table, no second manifest list, and no lookup in the registry's installed-package record. A lookup would also stamp a tenant row that is merely bound to a package (`registerObject(..., layer.packageId, undefined, 'own' | 'overlay')` from the stored-row hydration) with a version it was never shipped at.

The callers that hold a package's manifest pass its version:

- `ObjectQL.registerApp(manifest)` reads `manifest.version` once and passes it to every stamping call it makes: owned objects (array and map), object extensions, apps, the manifest-as-app, `registerMetadataCollections` (every metadata collection, including the expanded view items and the `viewItems` channel), seed datasets, and `registerPlugin`. A nested plugin's objects, app and collections carry the parent's version, because the parent is their owning package (the same reason they carry the parent's id).
- `ObjectQLPlugin`'s residual registration (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects`, landed from main in PR #22701 after this card was dispatched) now passes `unclaimedTopLevel(stack).ownerVersion`. That is the same `(ownerId, ownerVersion)` pair the metadata door stamps the residual with. It is the only change in `plugin.ts`.

## Callers that have no version, and stamp the id alone

`applyProtection` never invents a version, so these are unchanged:

- `SchemaRegistry.registerKind` and `registerItem('plugin', manifest, 'id')`: no package id at all.
- `ObjectQLPlugin.loadMetadataFromService`, `ingestReloadedObjects` and the per-object refresh, and `MetadataFacade.register`: they pass the item's own `_packageId`. An item that came through the artifact loader already carries `_packageVersion`, and `applyProtection` keeps it.
- The metadata-protocol stored-row paths (hydration, write-through, rollback): `registerItem` with no package id, or `registerObject` of a `_provenance: 'org'` row under its binding. These are tenant-authored, not shipped by a package version.
- plugin-security's built-ins (`registerBuiltinPositions` / `registerBuiltinCapabilities`): the plugin's own id.
- `ObjectQL.registerObject(schema, packageId, namespace)`: the public proxy, unchanged.

The comment above `registerItem`'s `applyProtection` call now says this instead of "identical lock state".

## Files outside the claimed surface

The claim named `registry.ts`, the registry's callers inside `packages/objectql/src/`, tests there, and one changeset. Two more files changed. Both are test pins that asserted the asymmetry this card closes, and both went red with the change:

- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts`: "the registry copy carries no `scope` (and no `_packageVersion`)". It now expects the registry copy to carry `_packageVersion: '3.0.0'`, the version the door copy carries.
- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-security-registrar.test.ts` (the control case): `expect(got.capability[0]._packageVersion).toBeUndefined()`. It now expects `'2.0.0'`. The comment says `scope` is the one key that still tells the raw copy from the door's.

`packages/objectql/src/engine.test.ts`: three `toHaveBeenCalledWith` call-shape pins on `registerObject` gained the trailing arguments. Two manifests gained a `version` so that the pins assert the hand-off.

## Tests

- New `packages/objectql/src/registry-package-version-stamp.test.ts` (5 cases):
  - An app and an object registered through `ObjectQL.registerApp` are served with `_packageVersion`. Read through the real list door (`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getMetaItems`) over the real registry; the engine is a `find`-only stand-in answering no stored rows.
  - An upgrade re-registered through the same door is served with the new version (1.0.0, then 1.1.0).
  - A nested plugin's object and a collection item (an action) carry the owning package's version.
  - A caller that knows only a package id stamps the id alone.
  - CONTROL: the artifact loader door (`MetadataPlugin._parseAndRegisterArtifact`, unchanged) stamps `{ _packageId, _packageVersion: '2.0.0', _provenance: 'package' }` for the same manifest, and the registry door serves an identical envelope.
- `manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`: the residual object carries the stack's version (`1.0.0`) beside its id.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` at `20ea8d3118` (the final head `d669c0308d` differs only in the changeset text): 396 files passed, 7767 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` at `20ea8d3118`: exit 0, test layer OK (40 files / 234 errors / 65 pinned signatures held, unchanged).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` at `963a0ce760` (before the merge of main): 347 files passed, 4922 tests passed, 19 skipped. After the merge, at `20ea8d3118`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` exit 0, and the two edited runtime files: 2 files, 15 tests passed.

## Reverse verification

Each leg was predicted before the run. Both used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from the committed state. The subject resolves from `src/` by relative import, so no build was needed. Each restore was proven: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

- A: `registerItem`'s call reverted to `applyProtection(item as any, { packageId })`. Predicted red for the app, upgrade, nested/collection and control cases, and green for the id-only case. Observed: 4 failed, 1 passed, exactly those.
- B: `registerObject`'s call reverted to `applyProtection(schema as any, { packageId })`. Predicted red only for the two object assertions. Observed: 2 failed (the served-object case and the nested-plugin object), 3 passed.

## Gates

- All 70 gate families that `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives for this diff ran at `d669c0308d`, and each exited 0. They are the dispatch's 54 plus 16 that the changeset and the tests add. `--ran` reconciliation: 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI. A narrowed run at `20ea8d3118` (later commits touch only the changeset): `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 8 changed `.ts` files reports 8 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. `ESLint.isPathIgnored` confirms each file is in the linted population. The config enables no type-aware linting (its own comment: no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Line budget

+201 / -41 across 9 files, against a suggested 150. Code: `registry.ts` +28/-9, `engine.ts` +24/-17, `plugin.ts` +7/-4. Tests: the new file +107; `engine.test.ts`, the residual test and the two runtime pins +22/-11. Changeset: +13. Over the suggestion because the five-case test carries the cross-door control, and because the two runtime pins and the residual path were not known at dispatch.

## Acceptance notes

- `SchemaRegistry.updatePackageManifest` (the in-memory half of `PATCH /packages/:id`) can change a package record's `version` without restamping the items already registered. They keep the version they were installed with. This is a read-only inference; it was not exercised.
- The objectui follow-up objectstack-ai/objectui#12098 consumes this field. The rebuild-pending read is cloud's (objectstack-ai/cloud#2760) and is not in this PR.
